title: Treaty of al-Hudaybiyya
summary: In about 628 CE Muhammad set out from Medina to perform the lesser pilgrimage at Mecca, and Quraysh blocked him at al-Hudaybiyya. The sides agreed a truce, reported as ten years, with the Muslims returning the next year. The terms were seen as unfavourable, but the Quran called it a clear victory. No signed treaty survives, so details rest on later reports.

uncertainty.note: Conventionally 6 AH / 628 CE; sources differ on the month and no exact day is certain.

where.modern_name: al-Hudaybiyya, on the western approach to Mecca, Saudi Arabia (pin set at Mecca)
where.historical_name: al-Hudaybiyya, edge of the Meccan sanctuary, Hejaz

importance.justification: A truce between Muhammad's community and Quraysh that is read as recognising the community as an equal.

related.because: The truce later broke down, and Muhammad entered Mecca in 630.
